author: claude
description: Customers outside UTC keep asking why their morning report arrives in the middle of the night. Schedules now store an hour on the owner's wall clock plus an IANA `timeZone` instead of `hourUtc`. `nextRunAt` converts the local hour to UTC with `Intl`, validation rejects unknown zones, the email subject uses the local date, and the table gets `hour` and `time_zone` columns (missing zones default to UTC). Tests cover a Tokyo schedule, round-tripping through the table, and zone validation.

defects.mechanism: nextRunAt computes the zone offset once, at `after`, then reuses it for the target day and rolls over by adding a fixed 24 hours. When a DST change falls between the last run and the next one, the report goes out an hour early or late (9am instead of 8am in New York on the spring-forward day).

fromRecord reads the new `hour` column, but every existing row only has `hour_utc`, so hour is undefined and nextRunAt returns NaN. In runDue `NaN > now` is false, so every pre-existing schedule counts as due and its report is emailed on every one-minute cron tick.
